code:
echo $HOME

# Prints the value of the HOME variable, your home directory path

export OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434

# Creates (or overwrites) the variable OLLAMA_HOST and marks it for export

# "export" means child processes (like the ollama command) will inherit this value;
# the course container sets this same variable to the host.docker.internal address

export OLLAMA_MODELS=$HOME/ollama-models

# Tells the Ollama server where to keep downloaded models, if your home disk is small

env | grep OLLAMA

# env lists ALL current environment variables; grep filters to only OLLAMA ones

# Use this to confirm your variables are set correctly before launching a tool
description: Walk through inspecting environment variables with echo, setting child-process configuration with export, and verifying variables with env and grep.

steps.description: `echo $HOME` reads the `HOME` environment variable (the `$` prefix expands its value) and prints your home directory path.
`export OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434` sets `OLLAMA_HOST` and marks it for export so child processes you launch in this shell (such as `ollama` or `opencode`) inherit the address.
`export OLLAMA_MODELS=$HOME/ollama-models` combines `$HOME` expansion with `export` to point the Ollama server at a custom directory for downloaded model weights.
`env | grep OLLAMA` lists every exported variable in your current shell and pipes that list into `grep` to confirm both `OLLAMA_` settings are active before you start a tool.

title: Reading and exporting environment variables
